turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, this screen has frozen again. One second. Okay. You have come for Arjun?

[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes doctor, I am his mother. He is four years and two months, June born. From three days he is having fever and cough, and he is not taking food at all, even the curd rice he normally finishes he is pushing the plate away, and last night he was so warm I put the fan on full.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever and cough for three days. Sorry, how many days exactly? I was still typing the login.
[SEG0004] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Three days the fever. Cough is also there, more in the night.

[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It is not three days. I am his grandmother, I stay in the house and look after him. From Sunday he is hot. Today is Thursday, so five days. She was at her sister's place, she did not see the start.
[SEG0006] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sunday was only a little warm after he played in the sun. The proper fever is from Monday, three days. Kindly don't mix the days.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): So somewhere between three and five days, though you are not agreed. On the nurse's entry I see temperature 38.2 Celsius and weight 15 kilograms.
[SEG0008] person_3 (CAREGIVER): That 38 is less only. Before the auto I checked at home, 103 Fahrenheit, I did it two times.
[SEG0009] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It showed 102 Fahrenheit, not 103. You always take it on the higher side. And weight is not 15. Dr. Menon last month recorded 16.8, he is around 17 kilograms.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chart says one thing, you two say another. I will not overwrite it blindly. Is the nose running?

[SEG0011] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes, watery discharge, he keeps wiping it on my dupatta. And sleep is broken. Last night he slept only after one o'clock, woke at four, I gave Horlicks, two sips, then he wanted the ceiling light off, then on again.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did the cough start? Please repeat, I had opened the wrong visit.

[SEG0013] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I cannot put a date. A small cough has been there since Diwali or just after Diwali, I don't remember which. Now with the fever it is louder, and the nights are worse.
[SEG0014] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Diwali time it was a tiny cough, nothing. This fever-cough brings a little yellow phlegm in the morning. I saw it.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yellow in the morning only, or through the day?

[SEG0016] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Mostly morning. In the day it is more a dry cough, and if he runs a little, like from the hall to the bedroom, it comes more. He was playing with his red car yesterday and he had to sit down.
[SEG0017] person_4 (PATIENT): My throat is paining.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Throat is hurting, noted. Arjun, are you drinking water?
[SEG0019] person_4 (PATIENT): Dadi gave orange medicine.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): That wasn't what I asked, but okay. Mummy, what has he been given?

[SEG0021] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Only Crocin syrup, paracetamol 250 mg in 5 ml. One teaspoon, that is 5 ml, three times a day, for the fever. Measuring cap, not a kitchen spoon. Morning, afternoon and night.
[SEG0022] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Afternoon was me. I gave two spoons of Crocin, big spoon, because 5 ml does nothing at 103. And the orange medicine is Ibugesic. One spoon after lunch.
[SEG0023] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ibuprofen? I did not know. Last time the doctor said paracetamol only, not both together. We were not to give Ibugesic.
[SEG0024] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He was burning up, what else to do. One spoon only, after lunch. I am telling the truth.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Wait, I lost the dose, the window refreshed. How much paracetamol, again?
[SEG0026] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): From my side, 5 ml, three times a day. She says the afternoon dose was two spoons, so 10 ml. I was cutting fruit. I did not see the spoon she used.
[SEG0027] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Two spoons. Definitely. And one spoon of Ibugesic.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): So you are not agreeing the paracetamol amount, and I will not invent a single dose for what already went in. Any cough syrup?
[SEG0029] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ascoril LS, 5 ml, one time yesterday night. He vomited right after, so I stopped it completely. Not given again.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stopped after that one dose. The old amoxicillin prescription, did he ever take it?
[SEG0031] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Never given. The seal is still there in the fridge door. I did not want to start an antibiotic just for cold, so not a single dose.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Understood. Allergies to any medicine or food?
[SEG0033] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No allergies.
[SEG0034] person_3 (CAREGIVER): No, nothing.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Loose motions? A rash? Any more vomiting?

[SEG0036] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No loose motions. No rash, I looked at his stomach and his back this morning while bathing. Vomiting was only that one time after Ascoril. He is slightly dull, but he laughed at Peppa Pig, so what to say, not fully dull.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is he managing fluids? Sorry, say it clearly, someone is talking at the desk.

[SEG0038] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He is drinking water. Food intake is poor, biscuit and a little milk only. Also LKG called, they said keep him home with fever, two days already, and the teacher had sent a colouring worksheet which is still in the bag.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Arjun, does your tummy hurt?
[SEG0040] person_4 (PATIENT): I want to go home.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll leave the tummy question. Let me listen. One big breath, like a balloon.
[SEG0042] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest is clear, no wheeze. Throat is mildly red. Ears are fine both sides. Mouth is moist, so he is not dehydrated.
[SEG0044] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It is not pneumonia, no? The boy next door had pneumonia and was admitted, that is the only reason I rushed today itself instead of waiting.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): I think this is a viral upper respiratory infection with fever. I am not saying pneumonia. Examination is reassuring.
[SEG0046] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So you will not start an antibiotic?

[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): No antibiotic. Continue paracetamol, 5 ml of the 250 mg per 5 ml syrup, up to four times a day if the fever is there. Do not give ibuprofen again, and no extra spoon on top of the 5 ml.
[SEG0048] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Tonight I will not give Ibugesic, then.

[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): Correct, no Ibugesic. If the fever is still there after three days, or if he is breathing fast or not drinking, come back sooner. Otherwise I will review him in three days.
[SEG0050] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Review in three days, okay. Shall I bring the Crocin bottle so you can check the strength yourself?
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, bring the bottle next time. Keep giving sips of water. I have a call on the other line.
[SEG0052] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I will carry the bottle in my purse so it is not forgotten.
[SEG0053] person_4 (PATIENT): Home.

features: stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
